question: What is the primary role of a theoretical framework in nursing research?

options.A: To replace the need for data collection in clinical settings
options.B: To serve as the structural foundation and analytical lens for a study
options.C: To increase the financial cost of conducting academic research
options.D: To provide a list of medications used in patient care

explanation: A theoretical framework provides the structural foundation and a perspective through which researchers view, analyze, and interpret data. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why is a theoretical framework especially important for nursing in Nigeria?

options.A: It helps transition nursing into an evidence-based, scientifically grounded profession
options.B: It eliminates the need for ethical approval from hospital boards
options.C: It guarantees automatic publication in international journals
options.D: It completely replaces traditional nursing care plans

explanation: Understanding theoretical frameworks helps shift nursing from a task-oriented occupation to an evidence-based, scientifically grounded profession. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes a conceptual model?

options.A: A set of rigid mathematical equations used to calculate drug dosages
options.B: A loosely structured group of general concepts and ideas often shown in diagrams
options.C: An exact replica of a hospital ward used for simulation
options.D: A completely proven law of physics applied to surgery

explanation: A conceptual model is a loosely structured group of general concepts and ideas that often use diagrams to represent how they might relate. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h2)

question: How does a middle-range theory differ from a grand theory?

options.A: Middle-range theories are more specific and directly applicable to clinical practice
options.B: Grand theories are only used in laboratory animal testing
options.C: Middle-range theories are never used in academic research
options.D: Grand theories focus exclusively on single patient symptoms

explanation: Middle-range theories are narrower in scope, more specific, and directly applicable to clinical nursing practice compared to broad grand theories. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h2)

question: What primary role does a theoretical framework play during the research process?

options.A: It acts as a roadmap that guides every phase of the study
options.B: It replaces the need for data analysis software
options.C: It determines the exact budget required for fieldwork
options.D: It serves as the final conclusion of the research report

explanation: A well-defined framework acts as a roadmap that guides every single phase of the scientific process. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h3)

question: How does utilizing a theoretical framework help bridge the gap in nursing education?

options.A: By connecting classroom theory to practical bedside nursing care
options.B: By reducing the total number of clinical hours required
options.C: By eliminating examinations for student nurses
options.D: By focusing solely on hospital administrative duties

explanation: Applying theoretical frameworks helps bridge the gap between classroom theory and practical bedside nursing, leading to holistic patient care. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h3)

question: Which nursing theory focuses heavily on external environmental factors like ventilation and cleanliness?
explanation: Florence Nightingale's Environmental Theory emphasizes how external factors like ventilation, warmth, and cleanliness influence recovery. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory in nursing research?

options.B: Assessing how adults manage their own self-care needs during illness
options.C: Investigating the financial management of nursing schools
options.D: Studying the biological mechanisms of viral infections

explanation: Orem's theory posits that nursing is required when individuals are incapable of meeting their own self-care needs, making it ideal for chronic illness studies. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the first step a researcher should take when selecting a theoretical framework?

options.A: Consulting the hospital accountant for funding
options.B: Examining the research problem, questions, and study objectives
options.C: Randomly selecting a theory from a textbook index
options.D: Writing the conclusion chapter of the study

explanation: The selection process begins with a thorough examination of the research problem, questions, and objectives to understand what variables are being measured. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why must a chosen theoretical framework match the methodological design of a study?

options.A: To ensure logical consistency between the study approach and the underlying theory
options.B: To reduce the word count of the final research report
options.C: To satisfy formatting requirements for font size and spacing
options.D: To prevent ethical review committees from reading the proposal

explanation: The framework must logically fit the philosophical worldview and methodological design, such as aligning measurable variables with quantitative designs. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is a common mistake novice researchers make regarding theoretical frameworks?

options.A: Integrating the framework into every single chapter of the thesis
options.B: Treating the framework as an isolated section that is never referenced again
options.C: Using too many peer-reviewed journal articles in the literature review
options.D: Consulting clinical nurses before writing the proposal

explanation: Novice researchers often make the mistake of treating the framework as an isolated section in chapter two, failing to use it throughout the study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h6)

question: How should a theoretical framework be utilized during the data analysis and discussion phases?

options.A: To discard any unexpected or contradictory data results
options.B: To calculate the statistical mean and standard deviation automatically
options.C: To interpret why the results occurred and link findings back to the original theory
options.D: To format the reference list according to APA guidelines

explanation: During data analysis and discussion, researchers use the framework to explain why results occurred and whether findings support or refute the theory. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h6)

question: What constitutes the pitfall known as conceptual mismatch?

options.A: Selecting a framework that has no logical connection to the study variables
options.B: Using too many citations from Nigerian nursing authors
options.C: Failing to include a demographic questionnaire in the survey
options.D: Writing the research proposal in the wrong font style

explanation: Conceptual mismatch occurs when a researcher selects a framework that has no logical connection to the study variables or research questions. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h7)

question: How can nursing students best avoid complications when choosing a framework for a clinical project?

options.A: By choosing the most complex grand theory available regardless of the topic
options.B: By ensuring middle-range theories are used appropriately and seeking faculty mentorship
options.C: By avoiding the use of theoretical frameworks entirely
options.D: By copying a framework from an unrelated engineering thesis

explanation: Students can avoid complications by seeking faculty mentorship, critically appraising theories, and opting for appropriate middle-range theories. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h7)
